entries.title: Overview drag-and-drop & navigation polish
changes: Your cats now get about: they explore every perch, the window and the rugs, play and race round the house (kittens most), keep each other company, and rest in short, varied breaks instead of lying around. They still sleep at night, when tired and after a meal.
Settings > Data & advanced > Food database now has a Download button that fetches the USDA branded foods from GitHub (about 18 MB) and imports them, so you no longer need to pick a file.
Life Director: a long session name in the middle of the dial now wraps inside the ring instead of running past it.
Life Director: workout-plan sessions with an "&" in their name (like Active Mobility & Structural Recovery) now show a plain "&" instead of "&".
Life Director: a work shift or sleep that crosses midnight now draws as one solid arc on the dial, with no thin gap at midnight.
Returning to today now winds farther and takes longer based on how many days you travelled. A year away has a much longer rewind than a week away.
The winding date count, spring settle, and activity-ring reveal stay connected throughout the return.
Overview cards now reveal their destination with a smooth expanding transition from the tap, while the shared bars stay in place.
Press and hold an Overview card, then drag it to rearrange your dashboard. Cards lift, neighbors slide aside, and the layout saves when you drop.
The Edit button still manages hidden cards. Dragging near the screen edges scrolls the dashboard.
Life Director activity centers use compact, non-scrolling summaries and keep the main action visible. Dragging inside the center no longer scrolls the dashboard or top bar.

Hold a time on the Life Director’s outer track to schedule a pinned activity. The form starts at that date and time; moving your finger still rotates the calendar. Requires an already planned day and a free time slot.

Native Cat (beta): Play opens a toy tray right on the Cat tab. Pick a toy and a cat that feels like it comes to pick it up, carry it, toss it and chase it; a sleepy or hungry cat tells you why it won’t.
Native Cat (beta): two cats no longer lie on top of each other in one bed or stay in bed for hours, and after a meal a rested cat gets up and about instead of going straight back to sleep.
Native Cat (beta): the cats no longer rest hidden behind the sofa; resting spots by the sofa keep them in view.

Native Cat (beta): two cats now live together. They touch noses (and, while they are still strangers, hiss), chase each other, groom each other, curl up together for a nap and settle standoffs over a perch; a kitten follows the grown cat about. The Together card counts what they did, with the last moment and the pecking order, and “While you were away” mentions what they shared.
Native Cat (beta): the pale outline around the cats in the Overview card and the Cat tab is gone.
Native Cat (beta): a resting cat no longer shimmers. Its breathing is now a clean one-pixel lift, so the coat stays steady instead of popping and flickering.
Native Cat (beta): a sitting or sleeping cat’s tail no longer bulges below it for a moment; the tail stays resting on the floor in every frame.
Scrubbing along the bottom bar now keeps going when your finger passes over or ends on Quest. A scrub that starts on Quest still uses the older scrubber until Quest is native.
Native Cat (beta): cats now turn round step by step, through a three-quarter and a front view, instead of just flipping. It takes about a third of a second.

Native Cat (beta): cats no longer walk through the sofa. A cat crossing the living room goes round the sofa's front instead of sinking into its arm, and a cat on the cat tree's middle platform lies low instead of sitting with its head in the top one.

Native Cat (beta): when you feed the cats they go and eat again. Two cats fed together walk side by side to their bowls instead of sending each other away, a cat fed while jumping onto the sofa or a perch comes down to its bowl instead of eating up there, and a meal served from the Cat page, the voice or a link reaches the cats on the Overview card too.
Native Cat (beta): cats no longer poke through the cat tree. A cat scratches the post from in front of the tree, and one passing under its platform is drawn in front of it.
Developer: with developer mode on (Settings), the native Cat tab has a Demo parkour button that sends one cat on a climbing tour of the room; it changes nothing in your save.

Native economy check (beta): a new switch in Settings, Data & advanced, off by default. When it is on, the phone works out every XP and Sparks change the app makes itself (Logs, rewards, the shop, rest days, settings, quests, the Daily Hand, Health sync and the new day's decay) and only counts whether it got the same answer. It never saves or shows its own numbers, and nothing leaves the phone.

Native economy check (beta): the card under the switch says what the check is doing in plain words (checking, how many actions and how many came out different, paused for Battery Saver or an app update, or stopped and why) and when the last difference was. You don't need to do anything but use the app.

Native economy check (beta): Copy report puts a short summary on the clipboard to paste to the assistant (counts and field names only, never your activity names, notes or journal); Clear starts the counts again after asking; Save case… can save one difference in full to a file you choose, after a warning that the file holds your real data.

Native Life Director check (beta): a new switch in Settings, Data & advanced, under the economy check, off by default. When it is on, the phone also works out Life Director's plans, its week and what it saves, and only counts whether it got the same answer. It never saves or shows its own results, and nothing leaves the phone. Copy report gives a short summary to paste to the assistant (counts and field names only, never your goals or sessions).

entries.title: Life Director polish & update history
changes: Read what changed in Settings → Phone & sync → App updates → What’s new.
Unplanned dates show your sleep and work hours, with a message that the day hasn’t been planned yet.
Double-tap an empty corner outside the Life Director dial to return to today with a winding animation.
The date fades into your current activity while its colored ring draws around the dial center.
Dial rotation keeps following your thumb after it drifts away from the outer rim.
Switch Life Director sections by tapping their buttons; accidental sideways swipes no longer change sections.
